wizard.field.name: Name
wizard.field.interface: Interface of the relay host that faces the PC
wizard.hint.address: A broadcast address, or the PC's own IP address when the PC is in a routed network or another VLAN.
wizard.hint.command: Program and arguments; put quotes around parts with spaces. {host} becomes the PC's address, {mac} its MAC address.
wizard.ssh.generate: Create a new key for HomeLink
wizard.ssh.public_key: Public key (add it to the relay host or the PC):
wizard.ssh.openssh_missing: The OpenSSH client is not installed. On Windows 10 LTSC install it under Settings > Apps > Optional features > OpenSSH Client, then try again.
wizard.ssh.host_key_unknown: The host key of {host} is not known yet. Compare this fingerprint with the one on the device before trusting it:
wizard.ssh.scan_failed: Could not fetch the host key of {host}: {detail}
wizard.ssh.already_known: known_hosts already has an entry for {host}. HomeLink never replaces an entry. If the device was reinstalled and you are sure, remove the old entry with: ssh-keygen -R {host}
wizard.ssh.host_key_changed: The host key of {host} differs from the one stored in known_hosts. The device may have been reinstalled, or something else is answering in its place. HomeLink never replaces a key by itself.
wizard.ssh.trust_failed: Could not save the host key: {detail}
wizard.ssh.trust_done: The host key of {host} is trusted. Checking again.
wizard.rdp.note: HomeLink never handles the Remote Desktop password. Type it in the Remote Desktop window; Windows can remember it there.
wizard.wake.relay: Through a relay host over SSH (a router or an always-on device in the PC's network)
wizard.relay.setup.routeros: Run these commands on the router. They create a group that can only log in over SSH and run /tool wol, a user in it that can log in only from this computer's address, and import the public key. Replace anything in <angle brackets>. Not yet verified on every RouterOS version: check the result with the check on the last step.
wizard.relay.setup.etherwake: Run these commands on the relay host as root; the user must already exist. They install etherwake and add the public key to the user's authorized_keys. On OpenWrt use opkg install etherwake instead. If sudo is on, the last two lines let that user run this one program with sudo without a password. Replace anything in <angle brackets>.
wizard.relay.setup.wakeonlan: Run these commands on the relay host as root; the user must already exist. They install wakeonlan and add the public key to the user's authorized_keys. If sudo is on, the last two lines let that user run this one program with sudo without a password. Replace anything in <angle brackets>.
wizard.hint.sudo: Turn it on when the SSH user is not root and the tool needs root. HomeLink runs `sudo -n`, which never asks for a password, so sudo must be allowed without one.
wizard.magic.routed_help: To wake a PC in a routed network or another VLAN, use the PC's own IP address as the destination and add a static ARP entry for it (with its MAC address) on the router closest to the PC. A subnet broadcast address works only if that router forwards directed broadcasts.
wizard.test.note: The PC can be saved even if a check fails.
wizard.hint.windows_sleep: On Windows, sleep hibernates the PC when hibernation is enabled.
problem.host_invalid: {value} is not an IP address or a host name
problem.interface_invalid: {value}: use letters, digits and _ . - only, up to 64 characters, not starting with -
problem.interface_not_used: The {preset} preset does not use an interface
problem.address_not_used: The {preset} preset does not take a destination address
problem.user_invalid: {value}: no spaces or @, and not starting with -
problem.key_not_absolute: {value} is not a full path, for example C:\Users\me\.ssh\key
problem.conf_name: The file name {name} is not allowed: 1–32 characters from A–Z, a–z, 0–9 and _=+.-
problem.command_quote: A quotation mark is not closed
problem.command_braces: The curly braces are not balanced
problem.power_ssh_needs_both: Over SSH, sleep and shutdown go together: allow both, or use commands
problem.tunnel_in_use: Tunnel {tunnel} is used by: {pcs}. Remove these PCs or move them to another tunnel first.
